planning_basis: Entirely fictional preparation example. Day zero is a relative planning origin, not a meeting or an agreed kickoff. Duration bounds use calendar days and effort/capacity bounds use whole person-hours. No University fact, commitment, rating or resource approval is asserted.

findings.summary: Fictional release records do not consistently retain verification evidence.
Fictional recovery notes lack a repeatable end-to-end business verification exercise.
Fictional event reviews record discussion but not consistent follow-through.
Fictional AI experiment has no measured repair effort or repeatable evaluation yet.

recommendations.title: Establish release-evidence baseline
recommendations.outcome: A repeatable release record retains the change, verification result and responsible service role.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: Review three fictional release examples against the agreed record fields; later collect actual examples during the engagement.
assumptions: Existing change-record tooling can retain the fields without product procurement.
Named role has 24–40 whole person-hours available in this phase.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: A documented and repeated release practice may support a one-level progression.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Actual baseline assessment, repeated use, sampled outcomes and reviewer interpretation; dates alone prove no progression.

recommendations.title: Rehearse service recovery and verification
recommendations.outcome: An isolated rehearsal demonstrates restoration of the fictional submission workflow, not merely completed backups.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: Retained rehearsal timeline, dependencies, business verification and unresolved conditions; no live recovery action is performed by this kit.
assumptions: A representative rehearsal environment is available by relative day 60.
The supplied 40–60-hour role capacity is insufficient for this 70–90-hour allocation; the roadmap needs resourcing or scope revision.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: A repeated and evidenced restoration practice may improve operational maturity by one level.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Actual restoration evidence, recurring ownership, documented environment differences and a later repeat exercise.

recommendations.title: Close the event-review action loop
recommendations.outcome: Review actions have ownership roles, dispositions and evidence of follow-through.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: Trace two fictional review actions from observation to resolution evidence, preserving unresolved disagreement.
assumptions: This team can work independently of the release-baseline task; shared staff are still reviewed separately.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: Evidence of repeated follow-through may support a one-level progression from a documented practice.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Real review histories and recurrence evidence, not counts of meetings or individual employee scores.

recommendations.title: Review cross-group rehearsal lessons
recommendations.outcome: A shared improvement backlog preserves group-specific context and recurring conditions.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: Evidence-linked review dispositions and a verified change in at least one repeated rehearsal.
assumptions: Both prerequisites finish before this review starts.
The earliest start is day 80–100, so the preferred first phase is uncertain rather than guaranteed.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: Systematic cross-group learning is a one-level improvement hypothesis, not an average of group ratings.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Actual common findings, sustained review records and observable operational effects.

recommendations.title: Demonstrate a sustained operating cadence
recommendations.outcome: Repeated cycles retain decisions and show whether the selected practices help quality and reliability.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: Compare repeated evidence-backed cycles, including a counterexample and a justified change in approach.
assumptions: This package starts no earlier than day 180 so repeated-use evidence can be collected.
Only the stated whole person-hours are modeled; recurring workload beyond this package remains a separate estimate.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: Documented practice followed by repeated, evidenced operation is a two-level aspiration requiring separate validation.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Actual baseline, appropriate behavior anchors, sustained execution and outcomes; no automatic maturity uplift is calculated.

recommendations.title: Bound a useful AI-workflow experiment
recommendations.outcome: A bounded offline experiment identifies usefulness, repair effort and maintainability before expansion.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: An agreed synthetic task set, repeatable evaluations and recorded repair effort; no model service is called by this kit.
assumptions: Duration, effort and baseline are genuinely unknown; zero is not substituted.
A named owner role is proposed, not a staffing commitment.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: A target can be discussed, but improvement size is not assessable until baseline evidence exists.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Actual workflow inventory, baseline capability and measured experiment outcomes.

recommendations.title: Decide whether to broaden the AI workflow
recommendations.outcome: The organization chooses continuation, revision or retirement from the experiment's evidence.
recommendations.acceptance_evidence: Retain the evidence-backed decision, operating burden and unresolved comparison limits.
assumptions: An unknown prerequisite finish means this item's upper timing bound remains unknown.
Dependency independence never proves that enough specialist capacity exists.

maturity_hypothesis.rationale: No improvement level is inferred from completing a pilot or holding a decision meeting.
maturity_hypothesis.evidence_needed: Validated baseline and sustained practice evidence after any adopted change.
